mcq.QUESTION_DESC: Using residue theorem, the inverse Z-transform of \( \frac{z}{(z-1)(z-2)} \) (ROC |z|>2) is:
The residue at pole z=1 for \( X(z) = \frac{z^2 + z}{(z-1)^3} \) is:
For \( X(z) = \frac{z^3}{(z-1)^2(z-2)^2} \), the residue at the pole z=2 is:
Using residue theorem, \( Z^{-1} \left\{ \frac{z^2 - 3z}{(z+2)(z-5)} \right\} \) (ROC |z|>5) gives \( x(n) \) proportional to:

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Poles: } z=-2, z=5\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Residue at } z=-2: \lim_{z \to -2} (z+2) \frac{z^2-3z}{(z+2)(z-5)} z^{n-1} = \frac{5}{7}(-2)^n\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Residue at } z=5: \lim_{z \to 5} (z-5) \frac{z^2-3z}{(z+2)(z-5)} z^{n-1} = \frac{2}{7} 5^n\)

(2 Mark)

\(x(n) = \frac{5}{7}(-2)^n + \frac{2}{7} 5^n\)

(1 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Find the inverse Z-transform of } \frac{z^2 - 3z}{(z+2)(z-5)} \text{ using residue theorem.}\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Pole at } z=1 \text{ (double)}\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Residue } = \lim_{z \to 1} \frac{d}{dz} \left[ (z-1)^2 \cdot \frac{z^2+z}{(z-1)^2} z^{n-1} \right]\)

(2 Mark)

\(= \lim_{z \to 1} \frac{d}{dz} [z^{n+1} + z^n] = \lim_{z \to 1} [(n+1)z^n + n z^{n-1}]\)

(2 Mark)

\(= (n+1) + n = 2n+1\)

(1 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Find the inverse Z-transform of } \frac{z^2 + z}{(z-1)^2} \text{ using residue theorem.}\)

lq.ANSWER:
StepMarks

a) \(X(z) = \frac{z}{(z-1)(z-2)}\), ROC: |z|>2 (right-sided, so use contour outside |z|=2).
\(x(n) = \sum \text{Residues of } X(z) z^{n-1} \text{ at poles inside contour C (|z|=R>2)}\).
Poles: z=1, z=2. Both inside.
Res at z=1: \(\lim_{z \to 1} (z-1) \frac{z \cdot z^{n-1}}{(z-1)(z-2)} = \lim_{z \to 1} \frac{z^n}{z-2} = \frac{1^n}{-1} = -1\).
Res at z=2: \(\lim_{z \to 2} (z-2) \frac{z^n}{z-2} \cdot \frac{1}{z-1} = \frac{2^n}{2-1} = 2^n\).
So, \(x(n) = (-1 + 2^n) u(n)\).

(4 Marks)

b) \(X(z) = \frac{z^2+z}{(z-1)^3}\), ROC: |z|>1.
Pole: z=1 (order 3).
\(x(n) = \text{Residue at } z=1 \text{ of } \frac{(z^2+z)z^{n-1}}{(z-1)^3} = \frac{1}{2!} \lim_{z \to 1} \frac{d^2}{dz^2} [ (z^2+z) z^{n-1} ]\).
Let \(f(z) = (z^2+z)z^{n-1} = z^{n+1} + z^n\).
\(f'(z) = (n+1)z^n + n z^{n-1}\).
\(f''(z) = n(n+1)z^{n-1} + n(n-1)z^{n-2}\).
Evaluate at z=1: \(f''(1) = n(n+1) + n(n-1) = n^2+n + n^2 - n = 2n^2\).
Thus, residue = \(\frac{1}{2} \cdot 2n^2 = n^2\).
So, \(x(n) = n^2 u(n)\).

(4 Marks)

c) \(X(z) = \frac{z^2}{(z-1)^2(z-2)}\), ROC: |z|>2.
Poles: z=1 (order 2), z=2 (order 1).
Res at z=2: \(\lim_{z \to 2} (z-2) \frac{z^{n+1}}{(z-1)^2(z-2)} = \frac{2^{n+1}}{(1)^2} = 2^{n+1}\).
Res at z=1: For double pole:
\(\lim_{z \to 1} \frac{d}{dz} \left[ (z-1)^2 \frac{z^{n+1}}{(z-1)^2(z-2)} \right] = \lim_{z \to 1} \frac{d}{dz} \left( \frac{z^{n+1}}{z-2} \right)\).
Derivative: \(\frac{(n+1)z^n (z-2) - z^{n+1}}{(z-2)^2}\).
At z=1: \(\frac{(n+1)1^n (-1) - 1}{(-1)^2} = - (n+1) - 1 = -n-2\).
So, total residue: \(2^{n+1} + (-n-2) = 2^{n+1} - n - 2\).
Thus, \(x(n) = [2^{n+1} - n - 2] u(n)\).

(4 Marks)

d) \(X(z) = \frac{z^3}{(z-1)^2(z-2)^2}\), ROC: |z|>2.
Poles: z=1 (order 2), z=2 (order 2).
Res at z=1: Compute \(\lim_{z \to 1} \frac{d}{dz} \left[ (z-1)^2 X(z) z^{n-1} \right] = \lim_{z \to 1} \frac{d}{dz} \left( \frac{z^{n+2}}{(z-2)^2} \right)\).
Let \(g(z) = \frac{z^{n+2}}{(z-2)^2}\).
\(g'(z) = \frac{(n+2)z^{n+1}(z-2)^2 - 2(z-2)z^{n+2}}{(z-2)^4} = \frac{z^{n+1}(z-2)[(n+2)(z-2) - 2z]}{(z-2)^4} = \frac{z^{n+1}[(n+2)(z-2) - 2z]}{(z-2)^3}\).
At z=1: \(\frac{1^{n+1}[(n+2)(-1) - 2]}{(-1)^3} = \frac{[-n-2 -2]}{-1} = \frac{-n-4}{-1} = n+4\).
Res at z=2: Compute \(\lim_{z \to 2} \frac{d}{dz} \left[ (z-2)^2 X(z) z^{n-1} \right] = \lim_{z \to 2} \frac{d}{dz} \left( \frac{z^{n+2}}{(z-1)^2} \right)\).
Let \(h(z) = \frac{z^{n+2}}{(z-1)^2}\).
\(h'(z) = \frac{(n+2)z^{n+1}(z-1)^2 - 2(z-1)z^{n+2}}{(z-1)^4} = \frac{z^{n+1}(z-1)[(n+2)(z-1) - 2z]}{(z-1)^4} = \frac{z^{n+1}[(n+2)(z-1) - 2z]}{(z-1)^3}\).
At z=2: \(\frac{2^{n+1}[(n+2)(1) - 4]}{(1)^3} = 2^{n+1}(n+2-4) = 2^{n+1}(n-2)\).
So, total residue: \((n+4) + 2^{n+1}(n-2)\).
Thus, \(x(n) = [n+4 + 2^{n+1}(n-2)] u(n)\).

(3 Marks)
lq.QUESTION_DESC:
Find the inverse Z-transform of the following functions using the Residue Theorem (Contour Integration) method:

a) \(X(z) = \frac{z}{(z-1)(z-2)}\), ROC: \(|z|>2\)

b) \(X(z) = \frac{z^2 + z}{(z-1)^3}\), ROC: \(|z|>1\)

c) \(X(z) = \frac{z^2}{(z-1)^2(z-2)}\), ROC: \(|z|>2\)

d) \(X(z) = \frac{z^3}{(z-1)^2(z-2)^2}\), ROC: \(|z|>2\)
